t: Of the amounts made available for necessary expenses of the Office of Inspector General under this heading in Public Law 111–117, $1,800,000 are rescinded: Provided, That section 3002 shall not apply to the amount under this heading.

fable.w: This is a pure appropriations rescission affecting funds for a federal Office of Inspector General. There is no tempting participation reading: it mentions no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue. No party outside the federal government is involved in any federal decision.

opus.w: The section only cancels $1,800,000 of money already given to an Office of Inspector General and says that section 3002 does not apply to that amount. It has no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside groups or right to sue. Nothing in it is even on-topic for participation, so no supporting span is quoted.
opus.b: I'm labelling this "No". The only thing that might look procedural is the "Provided" clause, but it just stops section 3002 from applying to this money. It sets up no process involving anyone outside the federal government. The section rescinds funds from a federal Office of Inspector General, and no outside party takes part in any decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a budgetary provision that rescinds funds and excludes a specific statutory section (3002) from applying to those funds. It does not establish any process for consulting with or coordinating with parties outside the federal government. The reference to Section 3002 likely pertains to internal reporting or audit requirements, which are intra-governmental actions.
qwen_chat.s: Of the amounts made available for necessary expenses of the Office of Inspector General under this heading in Public Law 111–117, $1,800,000 are rescinded: Provided, That section 3002 shall not apply to the amount under this heading.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "section 3002" refers to a provision requiring public participation or consultation, and thus its exclusion is relevant. However, Section 3002 of Title 31 U.S.C. generally relates to the Inspector General's authority to report to Congress or conduct audits, which are internal government functions. Furthermore, the text itself is purely a budgetary rescission and does not describe any process involving outside parties.
